# Oral History Methods

Exploration cluster on how to interview people about the past, how memory works as evidence, and what a novelist owes the people whose stories she uses. Started in March 2025 before the [[dorothy-pengelly-interview-2025-04-23|interview with Dorothy Pengelly]].

## What lives here

- [[oral-history]], the background article, and the [[oral-history-workshop-2025-03-29|workshop at the Merrin]] run by [[ifeoma-clarke]].
- The method I used: [[run-an-oral-history-interview]].
- The consent record: [[dorothy-pengelly-consent-form]], and the governed pointer to the recording, [[dorothy-pengelly-interview-recording]].
- [[shared-authority]], the idea from the oral history literature that changed how I think about the interview.
- The open question: [[how-much-of-dorothys-story-can-the-novel-use]].

## Status

Dormant since mid-2025 apart from the consent question. Kept as exploration because the method interests me beyond The Salt Choir, possibly for book three.

## What I learned

The workshop and the interview taught me three things I had not expected. Preparation is mostly about consent and trust, not questions. The best material comes after a silence, not after a question. And the person you interview has a claim on what you make of them that does not end when the recorder stops, which is the uncomfortable centre of [[shared-authority]].

## Where it could go

A possible third book with more than one living memory behind it would need this properly: several interviews, a clearer agreement on use, perhaps a deposit arrangement with a museum from the start. If the [[third-book-option]] outline goes that way, this cluster becomes part of that project.

## Boundaries

No interviewee's personal details beyond what they agreed to share for the work. Recordings live outside the vault as governed pointers.
